title: 5 Hidden Risks of Legacy Insurance Systems
excerpt: Outdated insurance apps slow growth. Uncover how legacy systems impair underwriting speed, increase downtime, and harm policyholder retention.

toc.text: Outdated Insurance Applications: What are the 5 Risks You Can’t Afford?
How to Start Your Insurance Modernization Journey?

html:
Key Takeaways

  • 74% of insurance companies still rely on outdated systems for important insurance processes.
  • The consequences of legacy systems are high costs, security risks, and poor customer experience, alongside less reliable businesses.
  • The insurance digital transformation is crucial for increased scalability, agility and long-term competitiveness.
  • Taking a more insurance modernization approach ensures faster operations with better data usage and a seamless customer experience.

The real cost of legacy systems isn’t what you spend; it’s what you lose!

As today’s era is defined by heightened customer expectations and digital acceleration, outdated business applications are becoming strategic liabilities from mere inefficiencies. What was once the backbone of insurance operations is now becoming an obstacle to agility, innovation, and competitive differentiation, making insurance digital transformation a boardroom priority.

According to Earnix, 74% of insurers use legacy technology for at least some of the critical processes in insurance, including pricing, rating, and underwriting. At the same time, over half of insurers, or 52%, note legacy platforms as a significant barrier to growth and innovation.

Organizations anchored to legacy applications struggle with high operating costs, disjointed customer experiences, and rising compliance burdens. On the positive side, insurers who are visionary and have leveraged insurance cloud solutions are gaining agility, resiliency, and data accuracy.

That’s why insurance modernization is no longer optional; it is imperative.

In this blog post, we will explore the top 5 critical risks of running your insurance business on outdated applications and how you can embark on the journey of modernizing for long-term success.

Why Are Insurance Leaders Accelerating Digital Transformation?

The digital transformation of the insurance industry has become a strategic imperative mostly on account of market dynamics, changing customer expectations, and regulatory pressures.

Here are some of the big reasons why insurance leaders are moving towards digital transformation:

Outdated Insurance Applications: What are the 5 Risks You Can’t Afford?

Below are the 5 most critical risks that legacy systems may introduce to your insurance company:

1. The Cost Factor: When Legacy Systems Drain More Than They Deliver!

Do you know that, according to Kanopi, 70-80% of insurers’ IT budget is exhausted in maintaining the legacy systems? In addition to the infrastructure and licensing costs of outdated insurance applications, insurers have to bear some hidden financial drains, such as inefficient workflows, application downtime, manual processes, and expensive integrations.

Over time, such kind of inefficiencies add up to reduce overall profitability and discourage reinvestment in innovation. Contrary to this, modern technologies supported by insurance cloud solutions provide flexible and usage-based pricing models so that businesses can align their budgets with the actual needs. This ensures better financial control and enhanced ROI (Return-on-Investment) for the insurance companies.

2.The Experience Gap: Losing Customers Before You Even Compete!

The insurance sector has significantly evolved from a paper-based and product-centric to a digital-first and customer-centric ecosystem. Due to this, the customer expectations have shifted dramatically towards the following:

  • Instant support
  • Digital-first approach
  • Hyper-personalized experiences

This underscores that if your insurance company runs on outdated applications and avoids adoption of insurance digital transformation, it will become highly difficult for you to deliver seamless interactions across channels. There will be delays in claims processing, communications will be inconsistent, and customer journeys will be poor – all of which will ultimately drive your customer towards a more agile competitor.

3. The Silent Threat: Security, Compliance, and Reputation at Risk!

It is undeniably true that legacy applications are vulnerable to a cyberattack because they are minimally updated, use antiquated and weaker security protocols, and lack real-time monitoring capabilities. Also, compliance with new regulations is constantly needed, and legacy systems are always lagging in this aspect.

This creates a dual risk:

  • RISK 1: Financial penalties due to non-compliance.
  • Reputational damage from potential breaches.

To overcome these, insurance digital transformation methods, including insurance cloud solutions, can assist businesses in implementing advanced security layers, such as MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication), RBAC (Role-Based Access Control), Zero Trust, Microsegmentation, and more.

Read More: Securing Your Cloud: Azure Security Configurations Every Business Should Know

4. Innovation Paralysis: When Your System Can’t Keep Up with Your Ideas!

Particularly, a legacy system is usually a huge bottleneck for the insurance industry’s innovation. Because of its rigid architecture, it becomes difficult to plug in new innovative technologies, such as AI (Artificial Intelligence), ML (Machine Learning), NLP (Natural Language Processing), automation tools, and advanced Analytics.

As a result, innovation is slowed down, experiments become expensive, and many opportunities are lost in the process.

To solve this, collaborating with a reliable application modernization company assists insurers in adopting agile frameworks. It not only accelerates development cycles but also gives birth to innovative insurance products and services in the market.

5. Data Chaos: When Information Exists but Intelligence Doesn’t!

The insurance industry generates a massive amount of structured and unstructured data as follows:

However, outdated applications often operate in silos. This, in turn, makes it impossible to unite, analyze, or make good use of data. The outcome of this is disjointed insights, bad decisions, and lost opportunities in underwriting, customer personalization, and understanding risk. The insurance modernization dismantles these silos and translates data into actionable intelligence.

Evaluate how legacy systems are impacting your performance and security.

Identify Your Risk Exposure Today!

A Real-Life Example: How Legacy Systems Caused Operational and Financial Disasters?

The example below highlights a critical reality that without any insurance digital transformation, even industry giants are vulnerable to disruptions.

Ransomware Cripples Major Insurers (CNA Financial)

What Happened: In 2021, CAN Financial, one of the leading insurers in the USA, was hit by a ransomware attack in which the attackers accessed the internal systems. The company termed the attack a “sophisticated” one, as per TechTarget.

Impact: The attack forced CAN to shut down large parts of its operations for several days, including core operations like claims processing and underwriting. According to the reports, the company negotiated with the hackers and later on paid $40 million to regain control and access to its systems.

The company’s homepage had the following statement:

“Out of an abundance of caution, we have disconnected our systems from our network, which continue to function. We’ve notified employees and provided workarounds where possible. Should we determine that this incident impacted our insureds’ or policyholders’ data, we’ll notify those parties directly.”

The Legacy Factor: When the investigation was carried out, it was noted that the outdated and unpatched systems created vulnerabilities for hackers to breach the systems. The systems lacked the following:

  • Automated security updates
  • Advanced endpoint protection
  • Real-time threat detection

How to Start Your Insurance Modernization Journey?

Here is how you can successfully initiate their insurance digital transformation journey:

1.Perform a Full Technology Assessment: Begin with your current systems, their security holes, outdated applications, and any performance challenges.

2.Construct a Business-Driven Modernization Strategy: Insurance modernization efforts must constantly be aligned with business goals such as improving customer experience, growing revenues, and meeting compliance efforts.

3.Embrace Cloud and API-First Architectures:Attempt to embrace insurance cloud solutions to provide scalability and flexibility. You can also modernize your tech stack with API driven and microservices architectures to allow for faster innovation, deployment, and integration.

4. Engage the Right Modernization Partners:Don’t hesitate to work with the right application modernization company to mitigate risk and accelerate the speed of execution. With the real expertise, your insurance business can seamlessly start its journey to modernization.

5. Empower Data and AI-Driven Capabilities: Use data and apply AI capabilities to generate insights for fraud detection, insights for underwriting, and customer personalization.

6. Focus on Change Management and Workforce Enablement: Always equip your team with the right tools and training so that they can adapt to new systems seamlessly. If the adoption process is frictionless and strong, the insurance modernization can deliver real business value.

7. Start Small, Scale Fast: Always try to implement projects in small phases to test the impact before jumping to a large-phased implementation. It minimizes the risk and ensures that the entire transformation process remains steady.

Start your journey with a structured, low-risk approach tailored to your business.

Modernize Without Disruptions

Final Thoughts: From Legacy Burden to Competitive Advantage,/h3>

In the insurance industry, precision, trust, and speed define success. Therefore, if the applications are outdated, it can become a disastrous choice.

Legacy applications not only limit efficiency; they restrict innovation, expose security, and prevent insurers from delivering seamless digital experiences as per the customers’ expectations.

Therefore, insurance digital transformation is not only about updating your systems but also about staying ahead. By embracing continuous insurance modernization, insurers can get a resilient, agile, and scalable system. As we have explored the 5 risks, we realized why modernization is no longer optional.

The future belongs to insurers who can act early, because in this race, delay is the biggest risk of all.
